unlisted_practices: Policymakers should design value-based reimbursement models for generalist AI that tie payment to meaningful outcomes such as reduced hospitalizations or improved A1C levels rather than individual interactions.
Payers should create AI coordination billing codes that bundle multi-modal generalist AI analysis under a single payment, potentially scaled by level of service or technology provided.
Payers should adopt tiered reimbursement that scales payment with the level of AI involvement and autonomy, from assistive to augmentative to autonomous.
Policymakers should provide targeted government subsidies, similar to electronic health record adoption programs, to promote equitable distribution of AI in resource-limited healthcare organizations.
Reimbursement frameworks should incentivize AI systems that demonstrably improve care quality while minimizing excessive costs.
Reimbursement frameworks should require regular assessment of generalist AI performance, outcomes, and cost-effectiveness across diverse populations and clinical scenarios.
Policymakers should develop novel payment models that account for the evolving role of physicians as AI systems become more autonomous.

screen.reason: Commentary discussing reimbursement challenges, payment models, and policy/governance solutions for generalist medical AI systems.
